# Register reference {#registers}

This appendix lists the registers of LiteScope: the analyzer and the IO probe. It is
generated from the register definitions of the gateware, elaborated on a reference design
for the Arty A7 platform without running an FPGA toolchain. Offsets are in bytes from the
base of the bank; the base addresses depend on the SoC and are in the `csr.csv` of a
build. A LiteX SoC names the banks after the attributes that hold the cores, `analyzer`
and `io` in this design.

| Configuration | Target and options |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `arty_reference` | `digilent_arty` `groups: 41 and 4 bits` `depth=1024` `with_rle=True` `LiteScopeIO(8)` |

Access is `rw` for a register written by software (`CSRStorage`, or a `CSRStatus` that
software also writes, such as event pending bits cleared by writing 1), `ro` for a status
(`CSRStatus`) and `wo` for a write-only strobe (`CSR`). The reset value of a `CSRStorage`
register ends its description. A register wider than 32 bits takes several
32-bit words of the bus, most significant word first. The driver and `litescope_cli` use these names through the `csr.csv` of the build, so they
never need the offsets.

## Analyzer {#reg-analyzer}

Defined by `LiteScopeAnalyzer` (`litescope/core.py`).

The analyzer of this design has two groups: group 0 is 41 bits wide (an 8-bit counter,
a flag and a 32-bit word), group 1 is 4 bits wide. `data_width` is therefore 41, so the
mask and the value of a term take two 32-bit words each. With `with_rle=True`, a stored
word has 42 bits, the 41 bits of a sample and the marker bit, read as two sub-words.
`rle_enable` is absent from an analyzer built without `with_rle`; the other registers are
always present.

The widths follow the parameters of the analyzer: `data_width` for the term registers,
`bits_for(depth)` for the storage counters and at most 32 bits for `storage_mem_data`.
The bank takes the name of the analyzer attribute of the SoC, and the driver must be
given the same name ([Analyzer architecture](#analyzer-architecture)).

Bank `analyzer`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `mux_value` | `0x0000` | 2 | rw | Group to capture, `bits_for(ngroups)` bits; the trigger compares the samples of this group. Reset `0x0`. |
| `trigger_enable` | `0x0004` | 1 | rw | 1: arm the trigger, a term is consumed on each match. The falling edge flushes the terms left in the term memory. Reset `0x0`. |
| `trigger_done` | `0x0008` | 1 | ro | 1: term memory empty, every term matched or flushed (also 1 with no term loaded). |
| `trigger_mem_` `write` | `0x000c` | 1 | wo | Write: push the term (`trigger_mem_mask`, `trigger_mem_value`) into the term memory. |
| `trigger_mem_` `mask` | `0x0010` | 41 | rw | Mask of the next term, `data_width` bits: 1 for each bit the term compares. Reset `0x0`. |
| `trigger_mem_` `value` | `0x0018` | 41 | rw | Value of the next term, `data_width` bits, compared on the bits set in the mask. Reset `0x0`. |
| `trigger_mem_` `full` | `0x0020` | 1 | ro | 1: term memory full (`trigger_depth + 1` terms, `trigger_depth` a power of two of at least 4); a write is lost. |
| `subsampler_` `value` | `0x0024` | 16 | rw | Subsampling factor minus one: one sample is kept every `value + 1` cycles, `subsampler_width` bits. Reset `0x0`. |
| `rle_enable` | `0x0028` | 1 | rw | 1: run-length encode the samples from the trigger on. Only with `with_rle=True`. Reset `0x0`. |
| `storage_enable` | `0x002c` | 1 | rw | Rising edge: flush the storage and start a capture. Keep at 1 while reading `storage_mem_data`. Reset `0x0`. |
| `storage_done` | `0x0030` | 1 | ro | 1: storage idle, capture complete or never started. |
| `storage_length` | `0x0034` | 11 | rw | Words of the capture, pre-trigger window included, `bits_for(depth)` bits; at most `depth`. Reset `0x0`. |
| `storage_offset` | `0x0038` | 11 | rw | Pre-trigger window in words, `bits_for(depth)` bits; below `depth`. Reset `0x0`. |
| `storage_mem_` `level` | `0x003c` | 11 | ro | Words still in the storage memory, `bits_for(depth)` bits; read it once `storage_done` is 1. The last words of a capture, up to four, have then moved to the read path and are not counted. |
| `storage_mem_` `data` | `0x0040` | 32 | ro | Read port: next 32-bit sub-word of the capture, least significant first; each read pops it. |

## IO probe {#reg-io}

Defined by `LiteScopeIO` (`litescope/core.py`).

`LiteScopeIO` wraps a LiteX `GPIOInOut`: its registers have the width given to the IO
probe, 8 bits in this design ([IO probe](#io-probe)).

Bank `io`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `in` | `0x0000` | 8 | ro | GPIO Input(s) Status. |
| `out` | `0x0004` | 8 | rw | GPIO Output(s) Control. Reset `0x0`. |
